mechanism: Part 1 scaffolds MT5→EA→Flask→SQLite pipeline: Trade ORM (symbol, tickets, lot, entry, SL/TP, profit, open/close times, magic) and placeholder /api/v1/trades plus /analytics/summary routes; no market feature is computed.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Example symbols EURUSD/XAUUSD in schema notes; no live market series analyzed.
why_new_for_mis: Backend scaffold and API contract only — persistence infrastructure, not regime/vol/liquidity sensing.
quote: the workflow starts when MetaTrader 5 captures relevant trade data. The data is packaged in a structured format, sent to the Flask API via HTTP, and stored in the database

mechanism: EA OnTradeTransaction filters TRADE_TRANSACTION_DEAL_ADD with DEAL_ENTRY_OUT/OUT_BY, joins opening deal via HistorySelectByPosition, maps DEAL_REASON/DEAL_TYPE to strings, builds JSON, WebRequest POST; duplicate deal-ticket guard. Account journal export, not a market sensor.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Live test on XAUUSD H1 (0.10 lot manual close); bridge is account-level for any symbol.
why_new_for_mis: Closed-trade capture and HTTP bridge for a personal journal — no market regime/vol/liquidity feature.
quote: By capturing only closed trades, we ensure the data is final and complete. This avoids partial updates and guarantees that each record sent to the backend represents a fully resolved trade

mechanism: POST /api/v1/trades validates required JSON fields, parses open/close times as YYYY.MM.DD HH:MM:SS, casts numerics, commits Trade rows with rollback on failure; GET list/detail and trivial total_trades/total_profit summary. Storage/CRUD only.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Example payload XAUUSD closed SELL; any MT5 closed trade the bridge sends.
why_new_for_mis: Request validation and SQLite insert path — no MIS sensing of market state.
quote: The backend currently acknowledges incoming requests, but the data never reaches the database.... we will complete that final step by implementing the logic that processes incoming trade data and stores it inside SQLite.

mechanism: Aggregates stored closed trades into total_trades, total_profit, win/loss counts, win_rate, average_profit, and hold durations (close−open in seconds → avg/max/min); JSON /analytics/summary plus Jinja HTML dashboard. Trader performance reporting, not market sensing.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Six sample closed trades in local SQLite from MT5 bridge; symbols whatever was traded (series demo used XAUUSD).
why_new_for_mis: Own-trade P&L and hold-time scoreboard — strategy journal metrics, not MIS market regime/vol/liquidity sensors.
quote: These metrics are computed directly from the stored trade data and provide a compact summary of performance without introducing unnecessary complexity.

mechanism: Monte Carlo over synthetic positive-expectancy systems (win-rate×RRR grids) compares dynamic risk f×balance_{j-1} vs fixed f×balance_i at 1%/2%/5%; reports consecutive-loss min/median/max and equity/drawdown distributions. Risk-policy simulation given assumed win-rate, not a live market sensor.
data_needed: Assumed win_rate, RRR, num_trades, initial_balance, risk_percent; random win/loss sequence (optional seed).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: No market instrument — synthetic 500–1000 trade paths; systems at 30%/2.6, 50%/1.7, 65%/0.9, 76%/0.6, 83%/0.3.
why_new_for_mis: Position-sizing and ruin/drawdown education under Bernoulli trade outcomes — no regime/vol/liquidity sensing of price/liquidity data.
quote: we will develop a Monte Carlo simulation to dive deeper into the topic of position sizing.... model hundreds or thousands of possible trading outcomes based on a system’s win-rate, risk-reward ratio, and position size.
